THE BRIEF

A classroom, consultation space and community hall have different occupancy patterns. We use the facility’s operating requirements to plan access and separation, then confirm the building work, affected services and cleaning needed for the agreed area.

✺

PROPERTY IN USE

Three settings, three access plans

SettingWhat we confirm
EducationClass use, arrival and collection periods, occupied rooms and available holiday windows
Healthcare premisesReception and room use, nominated access, separation and the facility’s cleaning requirements
Community facilitiesBookings, events, public routes and the area available between uses

PROPERTY IN USE

Practical work across rooms and grounds

  • Rooms and amenities

    We scope doors, hardware, walls, ceilings, fixed fittings and agreed amenity repairs by room or location.

  • Access and agreed systems

    Lighting and access-related work is checked against the existing equipment and the spaces affected. Any service interruption is identified before attendance.

  • Outdoor spaces

    Grounds, pathways, gardens and agreed external fixtures are reviewed with public movement and material access in mind.

PROPERTY IN USE

Small repairs and planned updates

A single door fault or damaged wall can be defined as a local task. A longer room or grounds list can be grouped into stages, keeping each item and its access requirements visible.

For a larger update, we confirm retained items, materials, affected services and the sequence before finishes and clean-up. Specialist operational requirements are supplied by the facility and incorporated into the agreed building-work plan.

PROPERTY IN USE

Define the work zone before arrival

  1. 01

    Agree access and responsibilities

    We confirm the nominated facility representative, approved area, access restrictions and who can make decisions about changes.

  2. 02

    Separate work from daily use

    Material delivery, protection, noise, dust, waste routes and any temporary access changes are planned for the specific setting.

  3. 03

    Check the area for handback

    We record finished tasks, relevant operation checks, cleaning and any remaining conditions affecting reopening.

PROPERTY IN USE

Start with the room or grounds list

  • Describe each item

    Provide room names or site references, photographs, the symptom and known equipment or finish details.

  • Explain availability

    Include operating hours, bookings, access arrangements and any facility-specific work or cleaning requirements.

PROPERTY IN USE

A handover the facility can follow

We identify completed work by location and retain any outstanding material, decision or follow-up as a separate item. The facility manager can then confirm the next use of each area against the recorded work and reopening conditions.

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

Good to know.

Can you group maintenance into a holiday or booking gap?+

We review the work list against access, materials and the available period. Tasks requiring curing, a service interruption or a return visit are identified before the sequence is agreed.

What does healthcare maintenance cover here?+

We scope the agreed building and facility items such as rooms, doors, finishes, amenities and access. The facility supplies its operating and cleaning requirements for those work areas.

Technical reading

  • Queensland Health — Condition assessment — QH-GDL-354-1-2
